newsitem.title: USA: Shabazz battling for her life at N.Y. burn center.
newsitem.headline: Shabazz battling for her life at N.Y. burn center.

text.p: Betty Shabazz, widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, battled for her life on Tuesday as her 12-year-old grandson faced indictment at a court hearing on charges he set the fire that burned 80 percent of her body.

"She is still extremely critical. She's on a ventilator and is heavily sedated; otherwise she would be in too much pain," said Nina Johnson, a spokeswoman at the Jacobi Hospital Burn Unit where Shabazz, 63, is being treated for third degree burns.
"She's holding her own. She can stay in this critical condition for an indefinite period of time," Johnson added.
The grandson, Malcolm Shabazz, named after his controversial grandfather, Malcolm X, is expected to be arraigned on Tuesday afternoon in Westchester Family Court before Judge Howard Spitz.
The judge had granted a 24-hour delay in the hearing to allow his mother, Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz, to get to New York from her home in San Antonio, Texas, where she works at a local radio station.

Qubilah Shabazz was indicted in January 1995 on charges she plotted to kill Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, whom Betty Shabazz had accused of playing a role in her husband's 1965 assassination.
The indictment was dropped last month after Qubilah Shabazz completed two years of counselling.
Qubilah, who arrived in New York City about midnight, was rushed to the hospital by Percy Sutton, the family attorney and a close friend and adviser to the Shabazz family for 40 years.

Speaking of the boy, Sutton told reporters on Monday that young Malcolm was "just a child who's been through a lot of trauma in his life ... He loves his grandmother very much and he expressed that love for her. He said how sorry he is."
The boy has been detained at a juvenile facility and is being examined by psychiatrists.

Family friend Bill Tatum, publisher of the Amsterdam News, said on Monday that her grandson, who was staying with Shabazz, was alleged to have used an accelerant to start the fire by the front door of her sixth-floor co-op apartment in Yonkers, New York.
Shabazz was found early Sunday morning by neighbours at the apartment with her nightclothes in flames after she tried to put out the fire.

Tatum said that "after allegedly setting the blaze, the boy ran out of the building and was picked up by police, wandering the streets in the nearby community of Bronxville," a community about 20 miles (32 km) north of midtown Manhattan.
